newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - June 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - June 19.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Deputy Defence Minister Anuruddha Ratwatte says influential cabinet minister in former United National Party regime, Sirisena Cooray, detained for his safety as well as to prevent breach of peace in country.
Ports and Shipping Minister Mohammed Ashraff moves out of official residence and plans to boyott cabinet meetings to protest against recent cabinet reshuffle.
Tamil Tiger rebels kill 23 soldiers in ambush in northeastern Pulmoddai. Rebels attack army camp and police post at same time.

Police say they will detain anyone, irrespective of rank or social status, in their probe into activities of former cabinet minister Sirisena Cooray who has been detained on suspicion of involvement in conspiracy to jeopardise national security.

Sri Lanka loses nearly five billion rupees in potential earnings in geuda trade because of 37 million carats of geuda taken to Thailand for 2.5 billion rupees for heat treatment, National Gem and Jewellery Authority says.
Tamil Nadu government mulls plan to develop minor port of Colachel into container port to rival Colombo.
Lawyers for former cabinet minister Sirisena Cooray to file fundamental rights violation plea in Supreme Court today challenging his arrest.
